title_en: Hebei Huasui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. v. Wuwei City Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of technical secrets
ruling_gist_en: Breeding intermediate materials and inbred line parents formed in the process of crop breeding, unlike plant materials discovered in nature, are intellectual achievements resulting from the creative labor of breeders. They possess the characteristics of both technical information and physical carriers, and the two are inseparable. Breeding materials with commercial value obtained through breeding innovation activities may be legally protected as trade secrets under conditions such as being unknown to the public and taking corresponding confidentiality measures.

full_text_en:
Hebei Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. v. Wuwei Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of technical secrets

[Ruling Summary]

Breeding intermediate materials and inbred line parents formed in the process of crop breeding differ from plant materials discovered in nature. They are intellectual achievements resulting from the breeder's creative labor, having the characteristics of being both technical information and tangible carriers, and the two are inseparable. Breeding materials with commercial value obtained through breeding innovation activities may be protected as trade secrets under the law if they meet the conditions of being not known to the public and having corresponding confidentiality measures taken.

The growth of breeding materials depends on soil, water, air, and sunlight and requires field management. It is difficult for the right holder to achieve foolproof confidentiality measures for such crop materials. Whether the confidentiality measures are reasonable needs to consider the characteristics of the breeding materials themselves, and the standard should be such that under normal circumstances, the degree of prevention against disclosure can be achieved. Formulating a confidentiality system, signing confidentiality agreements, prohibiting external dissemination, and using code names for reproductive materials can, under specific circumstances, constitute reasonable confidentiality measures.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 147

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Wuwei Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. Address: Floor 1, Shop No. 115, Building 1, Huangtai District 2 Public Rental Housing, Liangzhou District, Wuwei City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Ren Xinwen, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Liang Shunwei, lawyer from Beijing Kaiyue Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hebei Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. Address: No. 3 Kuangji Road, Wanquan District, Zhangjiakou City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Ren Wenbin, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhan Jianjun, lawyer from Gansu Zhengding Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ding Feng, lawyer from Beijing Guangdu Law Firm.

The appellant, Wuwei Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bosheng Seed Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2020) Gan 01 Zhi Min Chu No. 61 rendered by the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) on July 15, 2021, regarding a dispute with the appellee, Hebei Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huasui Seed Company), over infringement of technical secrets. After filing and accepting the case on February 7, 2022, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on March 4, 2022. Liang Shunwei, the agent ad litem for the appellant Bosheng Seed Company, and Zhan Jianjun and Ding Feng, the agents ad litem for the appellee Huasui Seed Company, appeared before the court for the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Bosheng Seed Company's appeal requests: 1. To set aside the judgment of first instance and amend it to dismiss all claims of Huasui Seed Company; 2. To order Huasui Seed Company to bear the case acceptance fees for both first and second instances. The facts and reasons are as follows: (1) The inbred line parent "W68" involved in the case is the male parent of the hybrid corn variety "Wannuo 2000", a new plant variety. As an approved variety, the approval announcement of "Wannuo 2000" records that the variety was bred in 2009, with "W67" as the female parent and "W68" as the male parent for hybridization. The said approval announcement disclosed that "W68" was bred by hybridizing the Wan6 selection line with the Wan2 selection line, followed by six generations of selfing and selection. Therefore, "W68" has become known to the public and does not constitute a trade secret. (2) "Wannuo 2000" was first approved in 2014, and Huasui Seed Company has been producing and operating the "Wannuo 2000" variety since 2015. According to common knowledge in the seed industry, when Huasui Seed Company entrusts a seed breeding company to produce "Wannuo 2000", it does not provide "W68" to farmers for free. Instead, it sells the parent seeds to the seed breeding company, which then sells them to farmers, generally at a price of about RMB 12 per jin. This fact indicates that Huasui Seed Company and its interested parties have already sold "W68" as a product. Since "W68" is a publicly sold product, it cannot constitute a trade secret and does not possess the secrecy required for trade secrets. (3) Huasui Seed Company did not provide valid evidence to prove that "W68" was bred by itself and is entitled to protect it as its own trade secret. Reproductive materials with the same characteristics and traits as "W68" have been used in several approved varieties, casting doubt on Huasui Seed Company's standing as plaintiff in this case. (4) Huasui Seed Company did not take sufficient confidentiality measures to prevent "W68" from being known to others. Huasui Seed Company sold "W68" as a product to seed breeding companies for producing the hybrid "Wannuo 2000", and the seed breeding companies then resold it as a product at a markup to villages and farmers for planting. Although Huasui Seed Company signed confidentiality clauses with the seed breeding company, there were no confidentiality agreements between the seed breeding company and the villages or farmers, and the villages and farmers were not obligated to maintain confidentiality to either the seed breeding company or Huasui Seed Company. The court of first instance's finding that Huasui Seed Company had taken sufficient confidentiality measures based solely on the existence of a confidentiality clause between Huasui Seed Company and one seed breeding company is inconsistent with the objective facts. (5) The judgment of first instance set overly lenient conditions for protecting parental reproductive materials. If the right holder merely claims that the variety has been approved and the approval certificate records the name of the corresponding parental reproductive material, then protection can be granted indefinitely and unconditionally. This would unduly expand the scope of protection for parental materials, undermine the new plant variety protection system, and hinder innovation in new plant varieties. (6) Bosheng Seed Company used "W68" for scientific research, and its acquisition of the parent seeds had a lawful basis. The court of first instance ordered Bosheng Seed Company to deliver all its existing stock of "W68" corn seeds to Huasui Seed Company, which implies that Bosheng Seed Company has no right to use the parent seeds for scientific research. This clearly contravenes the legislative intent of the Seed Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Seed Law) and the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties of the People's Republic of China.

Huasui Seed Company argued in response: The judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact and correct application of law. The grounds of appeal of Bosheng Seed Company are untenable. It requests the court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. (1) "W68" is an excellent inbred line parent seed bred by Huasui Seed Company's breeders after years of continuous selection using the Wan6 selection line and the Wan2 selection line as base materials. It possesses excellent quality and unique trait characteristics, is not known to the public, can bring economic benefits to Huasui Seed Company, has practicality, and has been subject to reasonable confidentiality measures by Huasui Seed Company. According to Article 9 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law) and Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Trade Secrets, as a parent material of Huasui Seed Company's hybrid varieties such as "Wannuo 2000", "W68" constitutes a technical secret. (2) Bosheng Seed Company failed to provide evidence of the lawful source of its acquisition of "W68". The court of first instance correctly found that Bosheng Seed Company infringed upon Huasui Seed Company's technical secrets. (3) Bosheng Seed Company engaged in malicious disclosure of Huasui Seed Company's trade secrets, and its liability for damages should be increased.

Huasui Seed Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, which accepted the case on October 16, 2020. Huasui Seed Company's claims: 1. To order Bosheng Seed Company to immediately cease infringing upon Huasui Seed Company's technical secret of the corn inbred line parent seed "W68" and to return the existing stock of "W68" inbred line parent seeds to Huasui Seed Company; 2. To order Bosheng Seed Company to compensate Huasui Seed Company for economic losses of RMB 1.5 million; 3. To order Bosheng Seed Company to bear the preservation fees, travel expenses, attorney fees, appraisal fees, and litigation costs in this case. Facts and reasons: "W67" and "W68" are excellent corn inbred line varieties bred by Huasui Seed Company over many years, possessing good germplasm quality. The hybrid corn variety "Wannuo 2000", cultivated by Huasui Seed Company using "W67" as the female parent and "W68" as the male parent, obtained a new plant variety right on November 1, 2015, with variety right number CNA20120515.0. Huasui Seed Company has not publicly disclosed the corn inbred line varieties "W67" and "W68", nor has it permitted any third party to use them. Bosheng Seed Company obtained Huasui Seed Company's corn inbred line variety "W68" through improper means. On September 24, 2020, Huasui Seed Company applied to the Liangzhou District People's Court of Wuwei City, Gansu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Liangzhou District People's Court) for on-site evidence preservation of Bosheng Seed Company's "W68" seed samples. Bosheng Seed Company's conduct infringed upon Huasui Seed Company's technical secrets and it should bear corresponding liability. As the gains of Bosheng Seed Company from the infringement and the losses suffered by Huasui Seed Company due to the infringement are both difficult to determine, Huasui Seed Company claims damages of RMB 1.5 million from Bosheng Seed Company by reference to Article 73 of the Seed Law (revised in 2015).

Bosheng Seed Company argued in its defense: Bosheng Seed Company did not produce "W68" corn inbred line seeds. The seeds preserved by the Liangzhou District People's Court at the application of Huasui Seed Company were "Shengtiannuo No. 9" corn seeds that Bosheng Seed Company was trial-planting and developing. Trade secrets are technical information not known to the public, having commercial value, and subject to confidentiality measures taken by the right holder. The new plant variety right that Huasui Seed Company claims to hold is for the corn variety "Wannuo 2000", but Bosheng Seed Company did not produce "Wannuo 2000". "W68" is merely a virtual code name, and Huasui Seed Company has no evidence to prove that "W68" is a new plant variety protected by state authorization. Huasui Seed Company has no evidence to prove that Bosheng Seed Company infringed upon Huasui Seed Company's technical information. It requests the court to dismiss Huasui Seed Company's claims.

The court of first instance, upon trial, found the following facts: The corn variety "Wannuo 2000" was approved as a municipal crop variety by the Shanghai Municipal Crop Variety Approval Committee on April 18, 2014, as a provincial crop variety by the Hebei Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committee on July 25, 2014, as a provincial crop variety by the Guangdong Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committee on March 6, 2015, and as a national crop variety by the National Crop Variety Approval Committee of the former Ministry of Agriculture on September 2, 2015. All these approval certificates recorded the variety source of "Wannuo 2000" as "W67" x "W68".

On November 1, 2015, the corn variety "Wannuo 2000" was granted a new plant variety right by the former Ministry of Agriculture. The application date for the variety right was June 11, 2012. The breeders were Guo Shaochen and Guo Ying. The variety right number was CNA20120515.0. The variety right holder was Hebei Wanquan Huasui Special Corn Seed Co., Ltd.

On January 1, 2014, Hebei Wanquan Huasui Special Corn Seed Co., Ltd. formulated a confidentiality system, stipulating that the company's breeding technical materials, breeding samples, breeding parents, reproductive materials, etc., were company secrets and should not be disclosed. On January 3, 2014, the company signed confidentiality agreements with Guo Shaochen, Guo Ying, Ding Shoubin, and Zhou Hai respectively, stipulating that Guo Shaochen, Guo Ying, Ding Shoubin, and Zhou Hai were to keep confidential, during their tenure and for a certain period after resignation, trade secrets including seed breeding methods, breeding parents, technical materials for seed breeding, and reproductive materials. Upon resignation, they were to transfer all held trade secret materials and items to designated personnel and complete relevant procedures, otherwise bear liability for breach of contract.

On August 18, 2016, Hebei Wanquan Huasui Special Corn Seed Co., Ltd. changed its enterprise name through industrial and commercial registration to "Hebei Huasui Seed Co., Ltd."

On January 1, 2017, Huasui Seed Company formulated a confidentiality management system, stipulating that the company's seed parents and research seed samples used for development and breeding, research technical materials, seed reproductive materials, etc., were company secrets and required corresponding confidentiality measures; they should not be disclosed. On January 5, 2017, Huasui Seed Company signed confidentiality agreements with Guo Shaochen, Guo Ying, Ding Shoubin, and Zhou Hai respectively, stipulating that Guo Shaochen, Guo Ying, Ding Shoubin, and Zhou Hai were to maintain confidentiality of Huasui Seed Company's trade secrets during their tenure and after resignation. The trade secrets included technical achievements and commercial achievements completed during their tenure while executing company tasks or using company conditions and information.

On September 12, 2020, Huasui Seed Company signed an entrusted breeding contract with a third party, Gansu Jinyuan Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinyuan Seed Company), for breeding corn seed varieties with the name "209", etc. The contract stipulated that Jinyuan Seed Company would deliver all qualified seeds produced according to the plan to Huasui Seed Company, and could not withhold or sell them on its own, otherwise bear liability for breach of contract. Jinyuan Seed Company was responsible for maintaining confidentiality of the inbred line parent seeds provided by Huasui Seed Company and could not spread them externally. On November 13, 2020, Jinyuan Seed Company issued a certificate recording that the corn variety named "209" in the entrusted breeding contract was the "Wannuo 2000" corn variety.

On September 21, 2020, Huasui Seed Company applied to the Liangzhou District People's Court for pre-litigation evidence preservation. On September 22, 2020, the Liangzhou District People's Court issued civil ruling (2020) Gan 0602 Zheng Bao No. 2, ordering the sampling of corn being bred by Bosheng Seed Company and the preservation of evidence including the entrusted seed production contracts, seed production area calculation sheets, detasseling and impurity removal acceptance sheets, parent seed issuance sheets, seed production acquisition quantity sheets, seed payment commitments, seed acquisition and warehousing forms, etc., held by Bosheng Seed Company.

Huasui Seed Company applied to the court of first instance to retrieve the samples preserved by the Liangzhou District People's Court and the video of on-site sampling. On October 21, 2020, the court of first instance issued a letter (2020) Gan 01 Zhi Min Chu No. 61 to the Liangzhou District People's Court requesting assistance in retrieving evidence. The Liangzhou District People's Court sent the evidence preservation samples by mail to the court of first instance. The samples were presented at the trial of first instance, sealed in two archive bags containing several corn ears. The seals of the archive bags bore the seal of the Liangzhou District People's Court, dated September 24, 2020, and were stamped with the court's seal. On one archive bag, "Main Plant" was written on the seal, with signatures of the executing officer and clerk. Under "persons present", there were signatures of "Ren Xinwen" and "Zhan Jianjun". Under "sampler", there was a signature of "Pan Mingcai". On the other archive bag, "Drying Ground" was written on the seal, with signatures of the executing officer and clerk. Under "persons present", there was a signature of "Zhao Yanlin". Under "sampler", there were signatures of "Pan Mingcai" and "Zhan Jianjun". Because the bottoms of both mailed archive bags were partially damaged, after the parties examined and cross-examined the bags at the first instance trial, the court of first instance resealed the bags and had the parties sign to confirm. During the first instance trial, Huasui Seed Company applied for an authenticity appraisal comparing the preserved sample from the bag marked "Main Plant" with "W68".

On May 25, 2021, the court of first instance requested from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs the retrieval of the standard sample of the male parent "W68" of "Wannuo 2000". After review by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, on June 9, 2021, the court of first instance retrieved from the National Crop Germplasm Conservation Center of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences the standard sample of the male parent "W68" of "Wannuo 2000". On the same day, the sample was submitted to the Beijing Maize Seed Testing Center for an authenticity appraisal comparing it with the corn sample from the archive bag marked "Main Plant" preserved as evidence by the Liangzhou District People's Court. The Beijing Maize Seed Testing Center issued inspection report No. BJYJ202100701257 on June 17, 2021. The report recorded that the number of comparison loci between the test sample and the standard sample of the male parent "W68" of "Wannuo 2000" was 40, and the number of different loci was 0. The inspection conclusion was extremely similar or identical. Huasui Seed Company paid the Beijing Maize Seed Testing Center an appraisal fee of RMB 5,000.

The court of first instance also found: On March 4, 2020, "Shengtiannuo No. 9" was approved as a major crop variety in Gansu Province by the Gansu Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committee. The variety source was "Bainuo 913" x "BSBai Tian 928". The applicant was Bosheng Seed Company and Wuwei Xianglin Seedling Co., Ltd. The breeder was Bosheng Seed Company. During the first instance trial, Bosheng Seed Company stated that the corn seeds preserved by the Liangzhou District People's Court were "Bainuo 913". The court of first instance asked Bosheng Seed Company whether it wished to apply for an authenticity appraisal comparing the corn seeds preserved by the Liangzhou District People's Court with "Bainuo 913". Bosheng Seed Company indicated that it would not apply for an appraisal.

Opinion of the Court of First Instance: In nature, the differences in traits between different plant varieties are determined by the genetic information expressed by the different genotypes contained in different plant varieties. The carrier of this genetic information is the reproductive material of the plant variety. A new plant variety is created by a breeder through long-term cultivation, reproduction, and improvement, embodying the breeder's skill and labor wisdom. The reproductive material of a new plant variety is the crystallization of the breeder's long-term labor wisdom and constitutes proprietary technical information belonging to the breeder. Because hybrid varieties are produced by crossing different parents, the parents contain the genetic information of the hybrid. The selection and breeding of parents are the decisive factors for the excellent traits of a hybrid variety. Once a new plant variety right is granted for a hybrid variety, the reproductive material of the hybrid variety is protected by the new plant variety right. The parents of the hybrid variety, because they contain the genetic information of the hybrid, constitute technical information and, if they meet the legal conditions such as confidentiality, constitute trade secrets and should be protected. The new plant variety involved in this case, "WanNuo 2000," is a corn hybrid variety. Its male parent "W68" and female parent "W67," as the parents of "WanNuo 2000," constitute technical information as stipulated in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. During the trial of first instance, there was no evidence showing that "W68" was a common corn variety that had been disclosed in the industry and was generally known to relevant personnel in the field of corn breeding. Therefore, the "W68" corn variety constitutes undisclosed technical know-how. According to Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Trade Secrets, if the right holder has taken measures such as entering into a confidentiality agreement or agreeing on confidentiality obligations in a contract, or proposing confidentiality requirements through charters or regulations, which under normal circumstances are sufficient to prevent the disclosure of trade secrets, it shall be determined that the right holder has taken corresponding confidentiality measures. In this case, HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. has submitted evidence proving that it has taken confidentiality measures for the "W68" technical information by entering into confidentiality agreements with the breeder of the new corn plant variety "WanNuo 2000," company executives, and entrusted seed production companies, and by formulating a company confidentiality system. According to appraisal, the corn sample taken by the Liangzhou District People's Court from BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is the male parent "W68" of the new plant variety "WanNuo 2000." Although BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. claimed that this corn sample was "ShengTianNuo No. 9," it did not submit corresponding evidence to prove this and did not apply for an appraisal. Therefore, its defense argument is not accepted. As a seed production company, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s use of HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s "W68" technical information in its production and business activities constitutes an act of using HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s trade secrets. During the litigation, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. could not explain the lawful and legitimate source of the "W68" technical information it used. Therefore, the court of first instance accepted HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s claim that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. obtained the "W68" corn inbred line variety through improper means. BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. shall bear the corresponding civil liability for infringing upon HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s trade secrets. According to Article 18 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Trade Secrets, if the right holder requests a judgment ordering the infringer to return or destroy the carrier of the trade secret, the people's court shall generally support it. Therefore, the claim of HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. cease the infringement and return the "W68" corn seeds in stock to HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is supported.

Regarding the amount of damages. Considering that "W68," as the male parent of the new corn plant variety "WanNuo 2000," has been cultivated for many years, has a high degree of innovation, and has relatively high research and development costs. Simultaneously, as an excellent corn inbred line variety, it can also be crossed with other varieties to form new corn hybrid varieties, possessing significant competitive advantages in business and capable of generating substantial commercial value. BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd., as a crop seed production enterprise that has been established for nearly 20 years, should be aware of the corn varieties it produces or uses and their sources. BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s use of the parents of a hybrid corn variety protected by a new plant variety right shows obvious subjective fault, and the nature of the infringing act is egregious. The court of first instance supports HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s claim for compensation of RMB 1.5 million in economic losses. The appraisal fee of RMB 5,000 paid by HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. constitutes a reasonable expense for HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. to enforce its rights, and the court of first instance supports this. Regarding the preservation fees, travel expenses, attorney fees, etc., claimed by HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd., because HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. did not submit specific evidence to prove these, and considering that this case has fully supported HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s claim for damages, the court of first instance no longer separately exercises its discretion to support the above reasonable expenses for enforcing rights.

Pursuant to Article 9, Paragraph 1, Items 1 and 2, and Article 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 152 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2017 Amendment), and Articles 1, Paragraph 1, 3, 6, Items 1 and 2, 9, 18, and 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Trade Secrets, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. Wuwei City BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease its acts of using the technical secret of the male parent "W68" of the corn new plant variety "WanNuo 2000," and return the "W68" corn seeds in stock to Hebei HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.; 2. Wuwei City BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the date the judgment takes effect, compensate Hebei HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. for economic losses and reasonable expenses for enforcing rights totaling RMB 1,505,000; 3. Other claims of Hebei HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. are rejected. If Wuwei City BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. fails to fulfill its monetary payment obligation within the period specified in the judgment, it shall double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance pursuant to Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2017 Amendment). The case acceptance fee of RMB 18,300 shall be borne by Wuwei City BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.

During the second instance of this court, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. submitted the following two groups of new evidence to this court: The first group of evidence is Notarial Certificate (2022) GanZhangLinGongNei No. 112, intended to prove that "WanNuo 2000" and "NongKeNuo 336" used the same parent, and its parent belongs to public resources. This notarial certificate records that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. entrusted three parents to the Zhangye National Corn Seed Production Base Seed Quality Supervision and Inspection Center for testing, and attaches four variety authenticity inspection reports ZGZ20220122, ZGZ20220123, ZGZ20220124, ZGZ20220125, on-site work records, on-site photos and mobile phone screenshot photos, and a video disc. BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. claims that according to the above inspection reports, Parent No. 1 differs from Parent No. 2 at 26 loci, Parent No. 1 differs from Parent No. 3 at 17 loci, "WanNuo 2000" is produced by Parent No. 1 and Parent No. 2, and "NongKeNuo 336" is produced by Parent No. 3 and Parent No. 2. BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. argues that the above inspection reports can prove that the parent of "WanNuo 2000" might have been bred by others, not by HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. The second group of evidence is the variety approval certificate for "NongKeNuo 336," which states the parent combination of this variety is "ZN3" x "D6644-2". Combined with the first group of evidence, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. argues that there exists a fact that different entities simultaneously bred the same parent reproductive material and named it differently, used it for tissue culture, and produced hybrid varieties. The so-called secret fact that the parent combination of "WanNuo 2000" was not disclosed to the public or allowed for use by third parties does not exist.

HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. rebutted this in its cross-examination, arguing that the evidence submitted by BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. exceeded the statutory time limit for presenting evidence and does not constitute new evidence for the second instance. Regarding the three bags of bulk corn kernels involved in the notarial certificate in the first group of evidence, there is no evidence indicating their source, and they lack legality. The four involved inspection reports, which compare two sample seeds with one control sample "NongKeNuo 336," and compare two sample seeds with one control sample "WanNuo 2000," are not conducted according to the standard testing methods referenced in the inspection reports. The standard referenced in the inspection reports is "GB/T39914-2021 SSR Molecular Standard Detection for the Authenticity and Purity of Main Crop Varieties — Maize." This standard specifies one-to-one identification, not the identification of parent seeds of two varieties mixed with hybrid seeds of one variety. The inspection reports are not lawful. During the first instance proceedings, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. stated that the seeds preserved by the court were the parent "BaiNuo 913" of its self-developed "ShengTianNuo No. 9." In the second instance, it claims they are the parent of "NongKeNuo 336." This is contradictory, and the evidence submitted in the second instance proceedings should not be admitted. On the contrary, the appraisal report submitted by BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is sufficient to prove that it infringed upon the "W68" trade secret. According to the appraisal report, Parent No. 1 and Parent No. 2 are not different from "WanNuo 2000," proving that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. simultaneously possesses the male and female parents of the "WanNuo 2000" variety and uses them for the illegal production of the "WanNuo 2000" variety. The time of the evidence preservation by the Liangzhou District People's Court was 1 year and 5 months before the sampling time for the new appraisal report submitted by BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. The fact that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. was still able to use the parents for notarization and testing at that later time is sufficient to prove that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. profited from breeding the "W68" parent inbred line, also profited from directly crossing to produce the "WanNuo 2000" variety, and is a professional infringing company whose infringing acts continue to this day.

Regarding the probative force of the above evidence submitted by BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd., this court will analyze and determine it in conjunction with the disputed issues in this case.

HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. submitted the following 4 pieces of evidence to this court during the second instance: 1. The "Gansu Province Crop Seed Production Contract" signed in 2019 between JinYuan Seed Industry Co., Ltd. and the Villagers' Committee of Tuqiao Village, Banqiao Town, Linze County, Zhangye City, Gansu Province. 2. The "Ganzhou District Corn Seed Production Contract" signed in 2020 between JinYuan Seed Industry Co., Ltd. and the Villagers' Committee of Baijiagou Village, Daman Town, Ganzhou District, Zhangye City, Gansu Province. Both contracts stipulate that "all qualified seeds produced shall be sold to Party A, and Party A shall ensure that the provided parent seeds (original seeds) are not allowed to flow out or be retained" and "violations of the contract shall be dealt with according to the relevant provisions of the 'Management Measures for Gansu Province Crop Seed Production Bases'." 3. The "Management Measures for Crop Seed Production Bases of Gansu Province." Article 15 of these Measures stipulates: "It is prohibited for seed production, operation units and individuals who are not contracting parties to maliciously collude with seed-producing farmers to privately retain, resell parents (original seeds) or contractually agreed seeds." Article 21 stipulates: "If seed production, operation units and individuals who are not contracting parties maliciously collude with seed-producing farmers to privately retain, resell parents (original seeds) or contractually agreed seeds, the seed administration department at or above the county level shall confiscate the seeds and illegal gains obtained by both parties, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000 on each party." HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. argues that, combined with the evidence it submitted in the first instance proceedings and the above 3 pieces of evidence, it can be proven that HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. has taken reasonable confidentiality measures for "W68." 4. The "Variety Breeding Report" for "WanNuo 2000." It records that the variety source of "WanNuo 2000" is "W67" x "W68," and "W68" was bred by crossing the Wan6 selected line with the Wan2 selected line, followed by six generations of selfing and selection.

BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. argued in its cross-examination that it does not dispute the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the two contracts, but does not accept HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s proposition. Since "WanNuo 2000" has been produced from 2010 to the present, HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. only submitted the "Entrusted Seed Multiplication Contracts" for 2016, 2018, 2020, and 2021. In these contracts, "W68" was sold to the seed multiplication companies at a price of RMB 10 per kilogram. Although the two newly submitted seed production contracts of BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. do not specify the name of the parent, they also involve selling to farmers for planting at RMB 80 per mu or RMB 16 per kilogram. Since "W68" has already been sold at a price, it does not constitute a trade secret but rather a product that can be traded. The two seed production contracts also cannot prove that HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. took sufficient confidentiality measures to make the measures coherent, reasonable, and appropriate. Moreover, from these two seed production contracts, it appears that no confidentiality measures were taken regarding the parent reproductive material towards the villages or farmers. There is no objection to the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the "Management Measures for Gansu Province Crop Seed Production Bases," but BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. argues that in reality, for villages and farmers, parents are purchased by themselves, and selling them is a normal situation. The above provisions cannot be deemed as confidentiality measures taken by HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. The authenticity of the "Variety Breeding Report" cannot be confirmed, but the content of the above report would be disclosed in the variety approval announcement. The public knows the variety source of "WanNuo 2000" and also knows the breeding method of "W68." The breeding technical information of "W68" no longer has commercial value.

Both parties to this case have no objection to the fact that the variety source of "WanNuo 2000" is "W67" x "W68," and that "W68" was bred by crossing the Wan6 selected line with the Wan2 selected line, followed by six generations of selfing and selection. This court confirms this after review. Regarding the probative force of the other evidence submitted by HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd., this court will analyze and determine it in conjunction with the disputed issues in this case.

The facts found in the first instance are basically true, and this court confirms them.

This court holds that the alleged infringing act in this case is BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s act of obtaining and using the technical information of the parent "W68" of "WanNuo 2000," which was targeted by the evidence preservation measures taken by the Liangzhou District People's Court on September 21, 2020. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law revised in 2019 shall apply. Based on the parties' appeals and responses, the issues in dispute in this second instance are: whether HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. has the right to file this infringement lawsuit; whether the parent "W68" of "WanNuo 2000" meets the conditions for trade secret protection; whether BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. has committed acts of infringing trade secrets; and whether the judgment of the first instance ordering BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. to deliver all stored "W68" corn seeds to HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is correct.

(1) Regarding whether HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. has the right to file this infringement lawsuit.

BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. argues that HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. cannot prove that it is the right holder of the "W68" parent in this case, and thus it does not have the right to file this infringement lawsuit. In this regard, this court holds that corn breeding mainly includes inbred line breeding and hybrid variety breeding. In the breeding of hybrid varieties, the utilization of heterosis is usually the main focus, starting with the breeding of inbred lines. Breeding excellent inbred lines is the foundation for breeding excellent hybrid varieties. For the breeding of corn inbred lines, it generally starts from a single corn plant, and after continuous multi-generational selfing combined with selection, an inbred progeny system with consistent traits and relatively stable genetics is obtained. This usually requires 5-7 generations of continuous selfing and selection, combined with yield testing to ensure yield and quality advantages. The basic materials for breeding inbred lines can come from local varieties, various types of hybrid composite varieties, improved populations, or inbred lines selected from progeny of hybrid varieties. The choice of basic material is related to the germplasm resources base owned by the breeding unit, the breeding objectives, and the experience and technical level of the breeder. In this case, the variety approval announcement for "WanNuo 2000" records that the breeder of the "WanNuo 2000" variety, which was crossed using "W68" and "W67," is HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. also acknowledges that "W68" is an inbred line formed after six generations of selfing based on a cross between the Wan6 selected line and the Wan2 selected line. It can be inferred from the facts that HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. used "W68" as a parent to cross and breed "WanNuo 2000," legally holds the "WanNuo 2000" variety crossed with "W68" and "W67," and that "W68" underwent six generations of selfing and selection after the cross between the Wan6 selected line and the Wan2 selected line. The basic materials for breeding "W68" originated from the germplasm resources held by the breeding unit, HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. In the absence of contrary evidence, combined with the conventional practices in the field of corn hybrid breeding, it can be preliminarily proven that HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is the breeder, developer, or right holder of the male parent inbred line "W68" of "WanNuo 2000." Therefore, HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. has the right to file this infringement lawsuit regarding the parent "W68" of "WanNuo 2000."

In the second instance proceedings, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. submitted the inspection report it commissioned itself and a notarial certificate, intending to prove that "WanNuo 2000" uses the same parent as the non-party variety "NongKeNuo 336." Based on this, it argues that the parent of "WanNuo 2000" was bred by others, not by HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd., and therefore HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is not the proper plaintiff in this case. It also argues that "W68" belongs to public resources. In this regard, this court holds that the variety approval announcement for "NongKeNuo 336" records that the breeder is the Maize Research Center of Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences, and the variety source is "ZN3" x "D6644-2." BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. also acknowledges that the parent combination of this variety is "ZN3" x "D6644-2." However, the approval announcement for "WanNuo 2000" records that the variety source for "WanNuo 2000" is "W67" x "W68." A comparison based on this preliminarily indicates that the breeding parent sources of the two varieties are different. In the second instance, BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd., based on the inspection report it commissioned, claimed that the breeding parents of the two varieties are actually the same. However, this inspection report is an opinion issued by an institution commissioned by BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. itself, and its legality, the scientific nature of the testing method, and the authenticity of the control samples must be reviewed. Upon review, the source of the breeding parent samples involved in this inspection report is unknown. The inspection matter of detecting the source of breeding parents through hybrid seeds is different from the inspection matter of variety authenticity and purity on which this inspection is based. Because this inspection report lacks samples with reliable sources and lacks relevance to the fact that BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. seeks to prove, it cannot prove that the parent "W68" of "WanNuo 2000" is the parent of "NongKeNuo 336." Therefore, this inspection report lacks probative force, and this court does not accept it. Consequently, the inspection report submitted by BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. cannot negate the fact concerning the breeding source recorded in the variety approval announcement, cannot prove that the parent sources of the two different varieties are the same, and especially cannot prove that "W68" belongs to public breeding resources. This court does not support BoSheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s appeal ground that HuanSui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is not the proper plaintiff to file this infringement lawsuit.

(2) Regarding whether the parent "W68" of "WanNuo 2000" meets the conditions for trade secret protection.

According to Article 9, Paragraph 4 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law revised in 2019, a trade secret refers to technical information, business information, and other commercial information that is not known to the public, has commercial value, and for which the right holder has taken corresponding confidentiality measures. Based on the claims and defenses of the parties, whether the parent "W68" of "WanNuo 2000" in this case meets the conditions for trade secret protection mainly involves the following specific issues.

1. Whether the parents of hybrid varieties constitute objects of trade secret protection.

2. Whether "W68" was not known to the public and had secrecy at the time of the alleged infringing act

Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. appealed, claiming that Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. and its interested parties had sold "W68" as a product, and that Huasui Seed Co., Ltd.'s entrustment of a seed breeding company to produce seeds resulted in "W68" becoming a commodity publicly sold by farmers, and therefore "W68" did not constitute a trade secret. In this regard, this Court holds that a parental line is the core breeding material of a breeder and is usually not publicly traded or sold. Breeders typically entrust seed breeding companies to multiply parental lines for seed production, but the act of entrusting seed production is not an act of selling the parental lines. Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2021 Amendment) provides that a party has the responsibility to provide evidence for its own claims. Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. alleged that Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. publicly sold "W68" as a commodity, and thus bore the burden of providing evidence to prove this, but Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. did not submit any evidence to prove it. During the second-instance trial, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. stated that it could purchase "W68" seeds on the market at any time, but expressly refused to provide this Court with information on the entity selling "W68" seeds, making it difficult both to prove that the seeds allegedly obtainable on the market were indeed "W68" seeds, and to prove that such purchase channel was lawful. Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. did not adduce evidence to prove its claim that "W68" was a publicly sold variety or that "W68" had been popularized and applied; thus, the evidence was insufficient to prove that "W68" had escaped the control of Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. and was in a state readily accessible to the public.

Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. appealed, arguing that the approval announcement of "Wannuo 2000" disclosed "W68" and its source, making "W68" known to the public and thus not a trade secret. In this regard, this Court holds that whether "W68", as the subject matter of trade secret protection, is known to the public should be determined by whether it is generally known or readily accessible to persons in the relevant field, and the object of being known to the public should refer to the specific technical information content, not merely the name or code of the technical information. The right holder's actual control over the breeding material is key to utilizing its genetic information for breeding. Breeding materials that have not yet escaped the actual control of the right holder and for which confidentiality measures have been lawfully taken are difficult to satisfy the constitutive requirements of being generally known or readily accessible to persons in the relevant field, that is, they possess secrecy. In this case, "W68" is a breeding material not known to the public, primarily for the following reasons:

First, for selection breeding, starting from the first segregation generation of a hybrid, individual plants are selected and grown into plant rows, and through subsequent generations of selection, superior plants are selected from superior lines until a uniformly superior line is obtained. To facilitate tracking the history and genetic relationships of the lines, individual plants and plant rows in each generation are systematically numbered. "W68" is merely a number assigned to the breeding material, a code given by the breeder for the purpose of subsequent selection breeding during the crop breeding process, and it refers to the breeding material actually controlled by the breeder. Although a specific code such as "W68" represents the specific genetic traits formed by the breeder's selection and domestication of plant materials from nature, the specific genetic traits are carried in the crop material. The code detached from the crop material itself has no breeding value; actual control over the breeding material is the prerequisite for utilizing its specific genetic information. In the breeding process of creating variation, selecting variation, and fixing variation, the crop code is used only to mark the source of the genetic information. Merely by the disclosure of the name "W68" in the variety approval announcement, one cannot actually know, obtain, or utilize the specific genetic information carried by the "W68" breeding material. Since the results of breeding innovation are embodied in the specific genes of the plant material and cannot be separated from the plant material carrying the innovative results, disclosing the code does not equate to disclosing the genetic information of the crop material. Where the crop material has not escaped the breeder's control, the relevant public cannot actually know, obtain, or utilize the genetic information of the breeding material referred to by the code. Therefore, the act of disclosing the code does not result in the disclosure of the genetic information carried by the breeding material it refers to.

Second, the approval announcement records that "Wannuo 2000" was crossed with "W67" as the female parent and "W68" as the male parent, and discloses that "W68" was bred by crossing Wan 6 selected line with Wan 2 selected line and then selfing for six generations. This fact proves that the breeding source of "W68" has been disclosed, but it does not prove that "W68" itself is an easily obtainable breeding material that has lost the secrecy of not being known to the public. First, Wan 2 selected line and Wan 6 selected line, as crop materials used to breed parental lines, are, according to customary practice in the breeding field, the core competitiveness of crop breeders, and are usually not publicly sold by breeders; the public has difficulty obtaining them. Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. has no evidence to prove that Wan 2 selected line and Wan 6 selected line are public breeding resources. Without the breeding sources of Wan 2 selected line and Wan 6 selected line, it is difficult to carry out selection breeding to obtain the stable inbred line "W68". Second, cross-breeding involves stages such as selection and matching of cross parents, determination of crossing techniques and methods, and selection of offspring, requiring a large amount of seed selection and production work, and the results of crossing are not unique. In the process of creating a population with variation through crossing, then selecting variation within that population, stabilizing variation through selfing, and finally forming a pure line variety, each generation undergoes the steps of selecting variation and stabilizing variation. Therefore, even if Wan 2 selected line and Wan 6 selected line could be obtained, in the process of breeding the inbred parental line, the breeder faces a certain degree of uncertainty in the selection of offspring when choosing superior individual plants and plant rows. For corn seed production, even if the breeding source of the inbred parental line and the crop target are disclosed, the pure lines obtained by different breeders cannot be completely identical. Thus, even if Wan 2 selected line and Wan 6 selected line could be used for cross-breeding, the inbred line obtained would not necessarily be "W68". It cannot be inferred from the mere disclosure of the breeding source of "W68" that "W68" is already known to the public.

Third, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. appealed, arguing that the fact that "Wannuo 2000" was publicly sold caused its parental line "W68" to lose secrecy, claiming that "W68" could be obtained from the publicly sold "Wannuo 2000". In this regard, this Court holds that although a corn hybrid is obtained by cross-breeding its parental lines, based on the characteristics of corn hybrid breeding and current technical conditions, it is very difficult to reverse-engineer the parental lines from the hybrid. The difficulty of reverse engineering is positively correlated with the costs required; the higher the costs required, the greater the difficulty of reverse engineering and the smaller the possibility. Whether the fact that "Wannuo 2000" has been publicly sold can lead to the inference that its parental line "W68" has lost secrecy requires an examination of the costs required to obtain "W68" from "Wannuo 2000", so as to determine whether it is readily accessible. It is clear that separating the parental lines from the offspring and cultivating the parental lines is not something that an ordinary breeder can easily achieve without expending creative effort. Without professional sequencing and isolation of "Wannuo 2000", it is difficult to obtain its parental lines, and even more difficult to ensure that the obtained parental lines are completely identical to "W68". Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. also did not provide any evidence to prove that "W68" could be easily obtained from "Wannuo 2000". Therefore, the fact that "Wannuo 2000" was publicly sold cannot automatically lead to the conclusion that its parental line "W68" is readily accessible to the public, and certainly cannot lead to the conclusion that the parental line "W68" has lost secrecy.

3. Whether the right holder took corresponding confidentiality measures for "W68"

Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. appealed, arguing that Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. did not take sufficient confidentiality measures for "W68" and therefore it should not be protected as a trade secret. In this regard, this Court holds that if a right holder has taken reasonable confidentiality measures before the alleged infringing act, and under normal circumstances these measures are sufficient to prevent disclosure of the trade secret, the people's court shall determine that the right holder has taken "corresponding confidentiality measures" that constitute a statutory element of a trade secret. When determining confidentiality measures, the people's court shall consider the degree of correspondence between the confidentiality measures and the trade secret. Plants depend on soil, water, air, and sunlight for growth and require photosynthesis. "W68", as a breeding material inbred parental line, must be managed with reasonable cultivation and a certain scale of seed production. In field management, it is difficult for the right holder to take confidentiality measures for such crop materials that are foolproof. Therefore, whether confidentiality measures for technical information on breeding materials are reasonable should take into account the characteristics of the breeding materials themselves, and the determination of the reasonableness of confidentiality measures should not be overly strict; it should be at a level of prevention sufficient to prevent disclosure under normal circumstances.

In the first instance, Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. submitted its internal confidentiality system and confidentiality agreements signed with the breeder of the new corn variety "Wannuo 2000", company executives, and the entrusted seed production enterprise. Based on the evidence submitted by Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. in the second instance and reviewed by this Court, internally, Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. had a confidentiality system stipulating that the company's breeding technical materials, breeding samples, and breeding parental lines and other reproductive materials were company secrets and must not be disclosed. It also stipulated that relevant company personnel, during their employment and for a certain period after resignation, must keep confidential trade secrets such as seed breeding methods, breeding parental lines, and technical materials and reproductive materials used for seed breeding, and upon resignation must transfer all trade secret materials in their possession to designated personnel and complete relevant procedures, otherwise bear liability for breach of contract. Externally, the "Entrusted Breeding Contract" signed between Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. and the third party Jinyuan Seed Co., Ltd. (with which it had an entrusted seed production relationship) stipulated that the name of the bred variety should be coded, Jinyuan Seed Co., Ltd. shall deliver all qualified seeds produced according to the plan to Huasui Seed Co., Ltd., shall not withhold or sell them on its own, and shall keep confidential the inbred lines provided by Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. and not disseminate them externally. In the breeding contract under which Jinyuan Seed Co., Ltd. entrusted the aforementioned village committee to produce seeds, it was stipulated that the parental line seeds shall not be leaked or retained. It should also be noted that at the seed production base, the relevant administrative authorities require the entrusted seed producers to register, and the registration content must be complete, particularly requiring that the entrusted production contract is complete, the variety rights and parental line sources are clear, and the production variety and area are consistent with the contract. The above content is an obligation that the producer should perform when fulfilling the contract, and is also an obligation that small-scale seed producers should perform when fulfilling the entrusted seed production contract. Acts by the受托人 of an entrusted breeding contract, such as unauthorized expansion of the production and breeding scale,私自截留, private breeding and production, and theft of parental lines, are all illegal or non-compliant acts. Moreover, there is no evidence in this case that "W68" was illegally disclosed or disseminated by the entrusted seed production unit. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Trade Secrets, taking into account factors such as industry practices in hybrid breeding, the use of codes for breeding materials, and the degree of accessibility of seed production activities, the confidentiality measures taken by Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. to prevent the parental line from being illegally stolen, obtained, or improperly used by others meet the requirement of "corresponding confidentiality measures" as a statutory element of a trade secret.

In summary, "W68" is a subject matter eligible for trade secret protection under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. As a breeding material with breeding competitive advantages obtained through breeding innovation, it has commercial value, is not generally known or readily accessible to persons in the relevant field, and the right holder has taken corresponding confidentiality measures. It meets the constitutive requirements of a trade secret and shall be protected by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law according to law.

(III) Whether Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. committed the act of infringing the trade secret

Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. appealed, claiming that the alleged infringing seeds were lawfully obtained by it and were reproductive materials used for scientific research. In this regard, this Court holds that, first, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. has the responsibility to provide evidence to prove its claim that the alleged infringing seeds were lawfully obtained or produced through self-breeding. Regarding lawful acquisition, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. did not submit any transaction records or information on obtaining "W68", and the source of the breeding materials used for producing and breeding "W68" is unverifiable. Regarding self-breeding, as discussed above, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. had neither evidence to prove that it held the Wan 2 selected line and Wan 6 selected line used to breed "W68", nor evidence to prove that its alleged infringing seeds were bred from other breeding lines. Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. could not provide any purchase or self-breeding records for the alleged infringing seeds. Its appeal claim that "W68" was lawfully obtained lacks factual basis and is not supported by this Court. Second, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. argued that its planting of "W68" constituted a scientific research activity. However, it did not submit any breeding plans, breeding records, or entrusted breeding contracts related to scientific research breeding for the alleged infringing seeds. Moreover, in the legitimate use of reproductive materials subject to others' rights for breeding in scientific research activities, it must in principle be for scientific research purposes and shall not exceed the scale and quantity necessary to achieve the scientific research purpose. Considering the scale and quantity of "W68" planted by Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd., it is difficult to meet the above requirements. Third, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. intentionally concealed the true information of the alleged infringing seeds. During the first-instance trial, Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. claimed that the alleged infringing seeds preserved by evidence were the parental inbred line "Bainuo 913" of "Shengtiannuo 9", but in the second instance it claimed they were the parental line of "Nongkenuo 336". This shows that Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. engaged in improper conduct of concealing and disguising its expansion and production of the alleged infringing seeds. In summary, the appeal claim of Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. that its production and breeding of "W68" constituted a scientific research activity lacks factual basis and is not supported by this Court.

Pursuant to Article 32, paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, in civil proceedings for infringement of trade secrets, where the trade secret right holder provides preliminary evidence proving that it has taken confidentiality measures for the claimed trade secret and reasonably indicates that the trade secret was infringed, the alleged infringer shall prove that the trade secret claimed by the right holder does not belong to the trade secret protected by this Law. In this case, the alleged infringing corn ears obtained by evidence preservation were in two bags, respectively marked "main plant" and "drying ground". The former was compared with the standard sample of "W68" from the National Crop Germplasm Preservation Center of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, and the identification result showed consistent molecular detection sites. At this point, Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. had completed its preliminary burden of proof to demonstrate that its rights were infringed. Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd., as the alleged infringer, failed to provide effective evidence to prove that "W68" did not meet the protection conditions for a trade secret. On the contrary, the fact that the alleged infringing seeds it planted were "W68" indicates that it actually produced and bred "W68". Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. could neither submit evidence proving that the alleged infringing seeds were lawfully bred from the breeding source of "W68", nor prove that it self-bred the alleged infringing seeds identical to "W68". Taking into account the basic circumstances of crop selection breeding described above, it is sufficient to determine that the alleged infringing seeds were produced and propagated by Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. through improper means of obtaining "W68", and such act constitutes an infringement of trade secrets under Article 9, paragraph 1, items 1 and 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The first-instance court's determination that Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. constituted infringement of trade secrets is correct, and this Court affirms it.

It should be emphasized that the comprehensive application of multiple intellectual property protection methods such as plant variety rights, patent rights, and trade secrets to construct a diversified and multi-dimensional legal protection system for crop breeding achievements is in line with the current state of China's seed industry development. The plant variety system and the trade secret system differ in the mode of right creation, protection conditions, and scope of protection, and the right holder may choose different protection methods according to the actual situation. In the crop breeding process, breeding innovation achievements that meet the protection conditions for plant variety rights may be protected under the plant variety right system. At the same time, breeding materials such as parental lines of hybrids that meet the constitutive requirements for trade secrets may be protected under the catch-all protection of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Granting anti-unfair competition protection to breeding innovation achievements that have not obtained plant variety protection, under the condition that they qualify as trade secrets, is an inevitable requirement to encourage breeding innovation and is also the proper meaning of strengthening intellectual property protection. The law does not limit crop breeding materials to only plant variety protection to the exclusion of other intellectual property protections such as trade secrets. Granting trade secret and other intellectual property protection to crop breeding materials does not weaken the legal regime for plant variety protection, but rather complements and reinforces it. Of course, granting trade secret protection to crop breeding materials does not prevent others from breeding varieties through legitimate means such as independent research and development, nor does it hinder the freedom of scientific research activities. This Court does not accept Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd.'s claim that the first-instance court's unlimited and unconditional protection of parental reproductive materials would undermine the plant variety protection system.

(IV) Whether the first-instance judgment ordering Bosheng Seed Co., Ltd. to deliver all its inventory of "W68" corn seeds to Huasui Seed Co., Ltd. was correct

Based on the above analysis, Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s relevant conduct has constituted infringement of Huahui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s trade secrets, and it shall bear civil liability such as cessation of infringement and compensation for losses in accordance with the law. Regarding the issue of bearing civil liability in this case, although Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. appealed requesting the reversal of the first-instance judgment and the dismissal of Huahui Seed Industry Co., Ltd.'s claims, it did not raise specific appellate claims or grounds regarding the civil liability of immediate cessation of infringement and the amount of damages determined in the first-instance judgment. It only objected to the first-instance judgment ordering the delivery of all inventory "W68" corn seeds produced by Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. to Huahui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. Given that the finding of infringement is established, the accused infringer shall bear corresponding liability for infringement in accordance with the law, and the appellant did not raise specific claims or grounds on appeal concerning the immediate cessation of infringement and the amount of damages, and this Court has not found any obvious impropriety in the relevant content of the first-instance judgment, this Court will not conduct further review on this matter. The relevant findings and disposition of the first-instance judgment shall be upheld.

With respect to the inventory "W68" corn seeds produced by Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd., as previously stated, "W68," as a trade secret protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, possesses the characteristics of being both technical information and a tangible carrier. Article 18 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Infringement of Trade Secrets provides: "Where a right holder requests a judgment ordering the infringer to return or destroy the carrier of the trade secret and to eliminate the trade secret information under its control, the people's court shall generally grant such request." The first-instance judgment's order that Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. return all its inventory "W68" corn seeds to Huahui Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is not improper.

In conclusion, the appellate claims of Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd. cannot be sustained and shall be dismissed. The first-instance judgment found the facts to be generally clear and correctly applied the law, and it shall be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 18,300 shall be borne by the appellant, Wuwei Bosheng Seed Industry Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
